source.title: Derry Journal, 22 April 1927, p. 11 ("Tyrone County and Rural Elections: List of Nominations")
source.publisher: Derry Journal (via the Irish Newspaper Archives)
source.check: returned unopposed: named in the Derry Journal's list of nominations of 22 April 1927

note: Triennial election of Tyrone County Council, polled Wednesday 1 June 1927. Nominations were taken on Wednesday 20 April 1927, and the Derry Journal of 22 April 1927 prints the full county list division by division under 'Tyrone County and Rural Elections: List of Nominations'. It says 'Only three contests are threatened for the County Council' — Fintona, Aughnacloy and Carrickmore — but the result reports of 2 and 3 June record only two polls, so the Carrickmore challenger withdrew. Killeter is given in the article's text rather than the list, where no nomination was made and Mr. Robert Thompson continued. That makes twenty-six divisions. Dungannon does not appear in the 1927 list at all, although it appears in the 1930 and later returns; it was therefore not a county division at this election, and no member is invented for it. The polled divisions keep the recorded results of 1 June, with the nomination notice added as a second citation. One discrepancy is left on the record: the Belfast Telegraph of 2 June 1927 gives the new council as 25 Unionists and 10 Nationalists — thirty-five members — which is more than the twenty-six divisions printed here, while the Irish News of 10 June 1930 gives twenty-four. The council's total membership is therefore not settled by the sources read, though every division printed is recorded. Returned unopposed.
